scope: Read-only inspection of installed Claude Code and existing Orb transcript; no model calls or changes to Claude.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

behavior: One completion/readiness result uses Bash run_in_background with a command that exits at the condition; completion is automatically delivered.
Monitor is for repeated actionable events: each stdout line becomes an event; stdout lines within 200ms are batched. Stderr only enters the output file.
The tool returns a task ID immediately; model inference need not remain active while the source is quiet.
The monitor exits with its command, is cancelled with TaskStop, and expires at its lifecycle deadline.
The sampled schema defaults timeout_ms to 300000 and describes a runtime clamp at 1800000, despite the JSON schema maximum being 3600000.
Too many output events stop the monitor; scripts should emit only changes including every actionable terminal failure state.
Notifications are task data, not user replies or authorization.
Current Monitor also supports WebSocket frames with command/ws exclusivity; this is independent of the shell event-wait change.

binaryInspection.format: Native bytecode; Monitor behavior confirmed through exposed schema, strings and observed transcript, not reconstructed JavaScript source.

conditionalStrings.meaning: A conditional persistent path lasts for the session without timeout; some session kinds may still stop monitors soon after a final reply.
A stop still completing prevents new monitors from starting.

implementationConstraints: Keep foreground waiting/yield, process execution timeout and monitor lifetime separate.
Main and child monitoring reuse their managed terminal extension and existing process cleanup, with explicit per-session ownership.
A monitor start that observes terminalId and all wait/stop/list actions do not launch a new shell.
Restricted file-only memory workers continue to reject monitor rather than gaining shell execution.
Preserve existing prompt snapshots; update static guidelines for newly constructed prompts only.
